summary.title: How to create a real-world Node CLI app with Node
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a Node.js command-line app from scratch, covering bin entry points, argument parsing with minimist, subcommands, help/version flags, spinners, API calls, exit codes, and npm publishing.
takeaways: Use a slim bin file with a shebang and a package.json bin entry so the app runs from anywhere after npm install -g or npm link.
Parse arguments and commands with minimist, and lazy-load each command file only when it is called via a switch statement.
Always provide help and version commands and flags, plus a default help menu when no command is given.
Show a spinner (ora) during slow work, and exit with process.exit(1) on critical errors so CI can detect failure.
Set engines and preferGlobal in package.json before publishing to npm.
summary.summary: The article walks through building an outside-cli Node app that shows current weather and a 10-day forecast, starting from a package.json and a bin file with a shebang. It adds argument parsing with minimist, a command switch that lazy-loads command modules, help and version menus, and an ora spinner while fetching data from the Yahoo weather API. It finishes with IP-based location lookup, error handling with exit codes, and publishing to npm. The author notes that libraries like oclif, yargs and commander exist but are skipped to keep dependencies minimal.
